about: What would have to change for `have` to reach `want`.
A LIST on each side, because there can be more than one weakest answer.
Empty means that side already holds. On a plain ladder there is always
exactly one, so every case here has at most a single entry — the
ambiguous case needs a scale where two levels sit side by side, and that
is asserted in the unit tests rather than here.
The weakest answer is not `higher(have, want)`. That one works and is not
the smallest, which only shows up off a ladder.

coverage.criterion: each side short alone, both short, neither short, and both ends of the scale
coverage.why: one scale only; applying the answer and re-checking is asserted in the unit tests

cases.name: wanting everything raises only the ceiling
